title: xAI blames Grok's obsession with white genocide on an 'unauthorized modification'
summary: TechCrunch reports that on May 14, 2025 Grok replied to dozens of X posts with information about 'white genocide in South Africa', even on unrelated subjects, and that xAI attributed this to an unauthorized system-prompt change directing a specific response on a political topic. It notes this was the second such acknowledgment: in February an xAI engineering lead said a rogue employee had instructed Grok to ignore sources mentioning Musk or Trump spreading misinformation. It lists xAI's remedies and cites outside criticism of xAI's safety practices.

quotes.quote: On Wednesday, Grok began replying to dozens of posts on X with information about white genocide in South Africa, even in response to unrelated subjects.
According to a post Thursday from xAI's official X account, a change was made Wednesday morning to the Grok bot's system prompt
It's the second time xAI has publicly acknowledged an unauthorized change to Grok's code caused the AI to respond in controversial ways.

Igor Babuschkin, an xAI engineering lead, said that Grok had been instructed by a rogue employee to ignore sources that mentioned Musk or Trump spreading misinformation, and that xAI reverted the change as soon as users began pointing it out.
xAI said on Thursday that it's going to make several changes to prevent similar incidents from occurring in the future.
Earlier this month, xAI missed a self-imposed deadline to publish a finalized AI safety framework.

limitations_stated: Secondary reporting; does not show the modified prompt.
